question.problem:
Find the equation of the **normal** line to the polar curve $r={\theta }^{2}$ at $\theta =\frac{3\pi }{2},$ given that 

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=\frac{2\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta +\theta \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta }{2\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta -\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta }.
$$
question.worked_solution:
To find the equation of the normal line to a polar curve at a point $P,$ we follow four steps:

**Step 1**: Calculate the derivative $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}:$

In this case, we're given that

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=\frac{2\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta +\theta \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta }{2\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta -\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta }.
$$

**Step 2**: Find the slope of the tangent at $P:$

The slope of the tangent line is

$$
\begin{aligned}m & ={\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}|}_{\theta =3\pi /2} \\  & =\frac{(2\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{3\pi }{2})+\frac{3\pi }{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{3\pi }{2}))}{(2\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{3\pi }{2})-\frac{3\pi }{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{3\pi }{2}))} \\  & =\frac{2\cdot (-1)+\frac{3\pi }{2}\cdot 0}{(2\cdot 0-\frac{3\pi }{2}\cdot (-1))} \\  & =\frac{-2}{(\frac{3\pi }{2})} \\  & =-\frac{4}{3\pi }.\end{aligned}
$$

**Step 3**: Find the Cartesian coordinates of $P:$

We compute the $xy$-coordinates of $P$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & =r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  \\  & ={\theta }^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  \\  & ={(\frac{3\pi }{2})}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{3\pi }{2}) \\  & ={(\frac{3\pi }{2})}^{2}\cdot 0 \\  & =0 \\ {y}_{1} & =r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  \\  & ={\theta }^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  \\  & ={(\frac{3\pi }{2})}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{3\pi }{2}) \\  & ={(\frac{3\pi }{2})}^{2}\cdot (-1) \\  & =-\frac{9{\pi }^{2}}{4}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the coordinates of $P$ are $(0,-\frac{9{\pi }^{2}}{4}).$

**Step 4**: Using point-slope form, find the equation of the normal:

We find the equation of the normal as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}y-{y}_{1} & =-\frac{1}{m}(x-{x}_{1}) \\ y-(-\frac{9{\pi }^{2}}{4}) & =\frac{3\pi }{4}\cdot (x-0) \\ y+\frac{9{\pi }^{2}}{4} & =\frac{3\pi }{4}\,x \\ y & =\frac{3\pi }{4}x-\frac{9{\pi }^{2}}{4}\end{aligned}
$$
